answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce resource before it can earn rewards, and the protocol slashes that bond when independently checked work fails or identities are caught coordinating fraud. A newcomer can still join, but creating a thousand disposable identities now requires a thousand funded bonds; sharing one bond does not multiply voting or payout rights. The attacker pays real capital and risks losing it, turning a cheap sybil swarm into a costly voyage. A relic of trust or a falcon badge alone would not provide this deterrent.
